subject.title: feat(plugins): support per-agent plugin installation with --agent flag

question: Should OpenClaw expose per-agent plugin install records before per-agent plugin discovery, activation, cleanup, and security semantics are fully designed?
rationale: This PR changes plugin code execution and persisted install metadata in a way that can create misleading isolation unless maintainers define the product and security boundary first.

options.title: Pause for full scoped lifecycle design
options.body: Keep the linked feature issue as the canonical design target, then merge a complete lifecycle implementation with security and upgrade proof.

options.title: Narrow this PR to internal prep
options.body: Remove the public flag and persisted scoped records, keeping only maintainer-approved helper changes that do not alter user behavior.

options.title: Accept install-only scope
options.body: Merge the partial surface while explicitly owning global activation, asymmetric cleanup, and upgrade risk as follow-up work.

recommendation.title: Pause for full scoped lifecycle design
recommendation.body: Keep the linked feature issue as the canonical design target, then merge a complete lifecycle implementation with security and upgrade proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent plugin install/uninstall hardening history makes this the best available owner for the lifecycle and compatibility decision.
